title: 谒衡岳庙遂宿岳寺题门楼
title_en: Visiting the Temple of Mount Heng, Then Staying at the Mountain Monastery and Writing on Its Gate Tower
author: 韩愈

text_note.zh: 这里用通行本。古籍文本有几个字写法不同：“一径”作“一迳”，“杯珓”作“桮珓”，“掩映”作“掩暎”，意思都一样；“云曈昽”古籍作“云朣胧”，都是形容朦朦胧胧、不太明亮的样子。
text_note.en: This follows the commonly taught text. The old corpus writes a few characters in older forms: the words for "path", "divining cup" and "half hidden" all use variant characters with the same meaning. For the clouds being dim and hazy, the taught text and the corpus use two different but similar-looking words, read tóng lóng, with the same sense.

readings.zh: 读 dāng，“当中”就是正中间。
readings.en: Read dāng; dāng zhōng means right in the middle.
Read yìng, meaning to answer or respond.

readings.zh: “伛偻”读 yǔ lǚ，弯着腰的样子。
readings.en: Yǔ lǚ means bending the back.

readings.zh: 读 fǔ，指干肉。不读 pú（胸脯的脯）。
readings.en: Read fǔ, meaning dried meat, not pú (chest).

readings.zh: “菲薄”读 fěi bó，微薄、不丰厚。
“睢盱”读 suī xū，睁大眼睛看的样子。
readings.en: Suī xū means staring with wide eyes.

readings.zh: “侦伺”读 zhēn sì，暗中观察。不读 cì（伺候的伺）。
readings.en: Zhēn sì means to watch closely. Here sì, not cì as in "serve".

readings.zh: 读 jiào，“杯珓”是占卜用的器具。
readings.en: Read jiào; bēi jiào are divining blocks.
Read cháng, meaning for a long time.

readings.zh: 读 jiàng，“将相”指大将和宰相。
readings.en: Read jiàng; jiàng xiàng means generals and chief ministers.

glosses.zh: 五岳：中国五座著名的大山：东岳泰山、西岳华山、南岳衡山、北岳恒山、中岳嵩山。
glosses.en: wǔ yuè: the Five Great Mountains of China: Tai in the east, Hua in the west, Heng in the south, another Heng (a different mountain with a different character) in the north, and Song in the middle.

glosses.zh: 祭秩：祭祀的等级。秩，等级。
glosses.en: jì zhì: the rank of the sacrifices offered to them.

glosses.zh: 三公：古代朝廷里最高的三种官。古书说祭祀五岳的礼仪和对待三公一样隆重。
glosses.en: sān gōng: the three highest officials at court. Old rites honored the Five Mountains as highly as these officials.

glosses.zh: 环镇：围在四周镇守。
glosses.en: huán zhèn: standing guard all around.

glosses.zh: 嵩：嵩山，中岳，在今河南。
glosses.en: sōng: Mount Song, the Central Mountain, in today's Henan.

glosses.zh: 火维：南方。古人认为南方属火；维，方位、角落。衡山是南岳，所以这样说。
glosses.en: huǒ wéi: the south. People of old linked the south with fire; wéi means a corner of the land. Mount Heng is the Southern Mountain.

glosses.zh: 地荒：地方偏远荒凉。
glosses.en: dì huāng: the land is remote and wild.

glosses.zh: 足妖怪：有很多妖怪。足，多。
glosses.en: zú yāo guài: full of monsters. Zú here means many.

glosses.zh: 天假神柄：上天把神的权力交给衡山的山神。假，给予；柄，权力。
glosses.en: tiān jiǎ shén bǐng: Heaven lent divine power to the god of Mount Heng. Jiǎ means to lend; bǐng means power.

glosses.zh: 专其雄：让它独自称雄一方。
glosses.en: zhuān qí xióng: so that it alone rules as the mightiest.

glosses.zh: 喷云泄雾：山中不断冒出云和雾。
glosses.en: pēn yún xiè wù: clouds and mist pour out of the mountain.

glosses.zh: 藏半腹：把山的半腰都遮住了。
glosses.en: cáng bàn fù: hiding the mountain's middle.

glosses.zh: 绝顶：最高的山顶。
glosses.en: jué dǐng: the very top of the peak.

glosses.zh: 穷：走到尽头，这里是登到顶上。
glosses.en: qióng: to reach the end; here, to climb to the top.

glosses.zh: 秋雨节：秋天多雨的时节。
glosses.en: qiū yǔ jié: the rainy season of autumn.

glosses.zh: 晦昧：昏暗不明。
glosses.en: huì mèi: dark and gloomy.

glosses.zh: 潜心默祷：专心地默默祈祷。
glosses.en: qián xīn mò dǎo: praying silently with all one's heart.

glosses.zh: 若有应：好像得到了回应。
glosses.en: ruò yǒu yìng: as if there was an answer.

glosses.zh: 感通：感动神灵，和神相通。
glosses.en: gǎn tōng: to move the gods and reach them.

glosses.zh: 须臾：一会儿。
glosses.en: xū yú: in a moment.

glosses.zh: 静扫：云雾一下子散尽，好像被扫干净了。
glosses.en: jìng sǎo: the clouds cleared away as if swept clean.

glosses.zh: 突兀：高高耸起的样子。
glosses.en: tū wù: towering up high.

glosses.zh: 撑青空：好像把蓝天撑住。
glosses.en: chēng qīng kōng: as if holding up the blue sky.

glosses.zh: 紫盖：衡山的一座山峰。
glosses.en: zǐ gài: Zigai, a peak of Mount Heng.

glosses.zh: 连延：连绵不断。
glosses.en: lián yán: stretching on and on.

glosses.zh: 天柱：衡山的一座山峰。
glosses.en: tiān zhù: Tianzhu, another peak of Mount Heng.

glosses.zh: 石廪：衡山的一座山峰，样子像粮仓。
glosses.en: shí lǐn: Shilin, a peak of Mount Heng shaped like a granary.

glosses.zh: 腾掷：像在跳跃、奔腾，形容山势起伏。
glosses.en: téng zhì: leaping and tumbling, describing the rising and falling ridges.

glosses.zh: 祝融：衡山最高的山峰。
glosses.en: zhù róng: Zhurong, the highest peak of Mount Heng.

glosses.zh: 森然：让人感到肃穆、害怕的样子。
glosses.en: sēn rán: solemn and awe-inspiring.

glosses.zh: 魄动：心惊、心里受到震动。
glosses.en: pò dòng: the soul is shaken.

glosses.zh: 一径：一条小路。
glosses.en: yī jìng: a single path.

glosses.zh: 趋：快步走向。
glosses.en: qū: to hurry toward.

glosses.zh: 灵宫：神庙，这里指衡岳庙。
glosses.en: líng gōng: the god's palace, here the Temple of Mount Heng.

glosses.zh: 粉墙丹柱：白色的墙，红色的柱子。
glosses.en: fěn qiáng dān zhù: white walls and red pillars.

glosses.zh: 鬼物：鬼神。
glosses.en: guǐ wù: spirits and gods.

glosses.zh: 填青红：用青色、红色涂满。
glosses.en: tián qīng hóng: filled in with blue and red paint.

glosses.zh: 升阶：走上台阶。
glosses.en: shēng jiē: climbing the steps.

glosses.zh: 伛偻：弯腰，表示恭敬。
glosses.en: yǔ lǚ: bowing low out of respect.

glosses.zh: 荐脯酒：献上干肉和酒。荐，献；脯，干肉。
glosses.en: jiàn fǔ jiǔ: offering dried meat and wine. Jiàn means to offer; fǔ means dried meat.

glosses.zh: 菲薄：微薄的东西，指自己的祭品不丰厚。
glosses.en: fěi bó: a humble offering.

glosses.zh: 明其衷：表明自己的心意。衷，内心。
glosses.en: míng qí zhōng: to show one's true heart.

glosses.zh: 庙令：管理庙宇的官员。
glosses.en: miào lìng: the official in charge of the temple.

glosses.zh: 睢盱：睁大眼睛看。
glosses.en: suī xū: staring with wide eyes.

glosses.zh: 侦伺：暗中观察、揣摩人的心思。
glosses.en: zhēn sì: watching closely to guess what the visitor wants.

glosses.zh: 鞠躬：弯腰行礼，表示恭敬。
glosses.en: jū gōng: to bow.

glosses.zh: 杯珓：一种占卜用具，用两片蚌壳或竹木做成，扔到地上，看正反面来判断吉凶。
glosses.en: bēi jiào: divining blocks: two pieces of shell or wood thrown on the ground; how they land tells good or bad luck.

glosses.zh: 导我掷：教我怎么扔。
glosses.en: dǎo wǒ zhì: showed me how to throw them.

glosses.zh: 余难同：别的卦都比不上。
glosses.en: yú nán tóng: no other result could match it.

glosses.zh: 窜逐：被贬官，赶到远方。
glosses.en: cuàn zhú: banished, sent far away.

glosses.zh: 蛮荒：偏远荒凉的南方。
glosses.en: mán huāng: the wild, faraway south.

glosses.zh: 甘长终：甘愿就这样过完一生。
glosses.en: gān cháng zhōng: content to live out my life like this.

glosses.zh: 侯王将相：封侯封王、做大将宰相，指大富大贵。
glosses.en: hóu wáng jiàng xiàng: lords, kings, generals and ministers: great wealth and rank.

glosses.zh: 望久绝：这个希望早就断了。
glosses.en: wàng jiǔ jué: that hope ended long ago.

glosses.zh: 神纵欲福：神即使想给我降福。福，这里是动词，降福。
glosses.en: shén zòng yù fú: even if the god wanted to bless me. Fú here is a verb: to bless.

glosses.zh: 难为功：也很难起作用了。
glosses.en: nán wéi gōng: it could hardly do any good.

glosses.zh: 投：投宿，找地方住。
glosses.en: tóu: to seek lodging.

glosses.zh: 掩映：时隐时现。
glosses.en: yǎn yìng: half hidden, now seen, now not.

glosses.zh: 曈昽：朦朦胧胧，不太明亮。
glosses.en: tóng lóng: dim and hazy.

glosses.zh: 曙：天亮。
glosses.en: shǔ: daybreak.

glosses.zh: 杲杲：太阳明亮的样子。
glosses.en: gǎo gǎo: bright, of the sun.

translation.zh: 五岳受到的祭祀，礼仪都和朝廷三公一样隆重，
translation.en: The Five Mountains are honored with rites as grand as those for the highest ministers.

translation.zh: 四座大山镇守四方，嵩山在正中间。
translation.en: Four stand guard on four sides, with Mount Song in the middle.

translation.zh: 南方偏远荒凉，妖怪很多，
translation.en: The south is remote and wild, full of monsters,

translation.zh: 上天把神的权力交给衡山，让它独自称雄。
translation.en: so Heaven lent its power to the god of this mountain to rule alone.

translation.zh: 山间喷出云雾，遮住了半山腰，
translation.en: Clouds and mist pour out and hide the mountain's middle;

translation.zh: 虽然有最高的山顶，谁又能登上去呢？
translation.en: there is a summit, but who can ever reach it?

translation.zh: 我来的时候正碰上秋天的雨季，
translation.en: I came just in the autumn rains,

translation.zh: 天色阴沉昏暗，一点清风也没有。
translation.en: the air dark and gloomy, without a breath of clear wind.

translation.zh: 我静下心来默默祈祷，好像得到了回应，
translation.en: I calmed my heart and prayed in silence, and there seemed to be an answer.

translation.zh: 这难道不是因为我为人正直，感动了神灵吗？
translation.en: Was it not because an honest heart can move the gods?

translation.zh: 一会儿云雾散尽，群峰都露了出来，
translation.en: In a moment the clouds were swept away and all the peaks appeared.

translation.zh: 抬头一看，高峰耸立，好像撑住了蓝天。
translation.en: I looked up: they towered high, holding up the blue sky.

translation.zh: 紫盖峰连绵起伏，连着天柱峰，
translation.en: Zigai Peak stretches on to meet Tianzhu Peak;

translation.zh: 石廪峰像在奔腾跳跃，和祝融峰堆在一起。
translation.en: Shilin Peak leaps and tumbles up against Zhurong Peak.

translation.zh: 我心里肃然一震，下马跪拜，
translation.en: Awed, my heart shaken, I got off my horse and bowed,

translation.zh: 沿着松柏间的一条小路，快步走向神庙。
translation.en: and hurried along a path between pines and cypresses to the temple.

translation.zh: 白墙红柱闪着光彩，
translation.en: White walls and red pillars glowed with color,

translation.zh: 墙上画满了鬼神，涂着青色和红色。
translation.en: and painted gods and spirits filled the walls in blue and red.

translation.zh: 我走上台阶，弯腰献上干肉和酒，
translation.en: I climbed the steps, bowed low and offered dried meat and wine,

translation.zh: 想用这点微薄的祭品表明我的心意。
translation.en: hoping this humble gift would show my true heart.

translation.zh: 管庙的老人好像很懂神的心意，
translation.en: The old temple keeper seemed to know the god's will;

translation.zh: 他睁大眼睛察看我的神色，很会弯腰行礼。
translation.en: he watched me with wide eyes and bowed most politely.

translation.zh: 他拿着占卜用的杯珓，教我扔下去，
translation.en: He held out the divining blocks and showed me how to throw them,

translation.zh: 说这是最吉利的一卦，别的都比不上。
translation.en: then said this was the luckiest sign, unlike any other.

translation.zh: 我被贬到偏远的南方，幸好没有死，
translation.en: Banished to the wild south, I was lucky not to die;

translation.zh: 只要有吃有穿，我就甘愿这样过一辈子。
translation.en: if I have enough to eat and wear, I am content to live out my days.

translation.zh: 当侯王、做将相的希望早就断了，
translation.en: My hope of becoming a lord or a minister ended long ago;

translation.zh: 神就算想给我降福，也很难起作用了。
translation.en: even if the god wished to bless me, it could do little good.

translation.zh: 夜里我住进佛寺，登上高高的楼阁，
translation.en: At night I lodged in the monastery and climbed its high tower;

translation.zh: 星星和月亮时隐时现，云色朦朦胧胧。
translation.en: stars and moon came and went behind dim, hazy clouds.

translation.zh: 猿在叫，钟声响起，我睡得不知道天已经亮了，
translation.en: Monkeys cried and the bell rang, and I slept on, not knowing dawn had come,

translation.zh: 明亮而带着寒意的太阳从东方升起来了。
translation.en: until a bright, cold sun rose in the east.

background.zh: 唐德宗贞元十九年（803年）冬，韩愈因为上书说关中旱灾、百姓受苦，被贬到阳山（今广东阳山）做县令。永贞元年（805年）遇到大赦，他离开南方，被改派到江陵（今湖北荆州）做法曹参军。这年秋天去江陵的路上，他经过南岳衡山，拜谒了衡岳庙，晚上住在山上的佛寺里，把这首诗题写在寺院的门楼上。
background.en: In the winter of 803, Han Yu sent a letter to the throne about a drought near the capital and the suffering of the people. For this he was sent away to be magistrate of Yangshan, in today's Guangdong. In 805 there was a general pardon. He left the far south and was given a minor post in Jiangling, today's Jingzhou in Hubei. That autumn, on his way there, he passed Mount Heng, the Southern Mountain. He visited its temple, stayed the night at a monastery on the mountain, and wrote this poem on the gate tower.

author_note.zh: 韩愈（768—824），字退之，唐代大文学家，“唐宋八大家”之一。他为人刚直，敢说真话，几次因为上书被贬。他的诗喜欢用奇特的字句和宏大的气势，常把散文的写法放进诗里。这首诗里有景、有事、有议论，正是他的风格。
author_note.en: Han Yu (768–824) was a great Tang writer, one of the Eight Great Prose Masters of Tang and Song. He was blunt and honest, and was sent away more than once for what he wrote to the throne. His poems like unusual words and a grand, bold sweep, and often borrow the style of prose. This poem mixes scenery, events and the poet's own opinions, which is very much his style.

appreciation.zh: 这首诗像一篇游记，按时间一步步往前走。先说衡山是南方的神山，又高又神秘，山腰藏在云雾里。诗人来时正下秋雨，天昏地暗。他默默祈祷，云雾竟然散开了，群峰一下子冒出来，好像要撑住天空。这一段写得最有气势，想象一下：灰蒙蒙的天忽然变亮，一座座山峰像在奔跑跳跃。接着他进庙献祭，庙里的老人帮他占卜，说是大吉。诗人却笑着说：我被贬到南方，能活下来就满足了，做大官的梦早就断了，神想保佑也没用。这几句有点自嘲，也有点倔强和不平。最后写夜宿寺中，星月朦胧，一觉睡到太阳升起，心情变得平静开阔。
appreciation.en: This poem reads like a travel diary, moving forward step by step. First the poet says Mount Heng is the sacred mountain of the south, tall and mysterious, its middle hidden in cloud. When he arrives, the autumn rain makes everything dark. He prays in silence, and the clouds actually part. All the peaks suddenly appear, as if holding up the sky. This is the grandest part. Picture a gray sky turning bright, and peak after peak seeming to run and leap. Then he enters the temple and makes his offering. The old keeper reads his fortune and says it is the best sign of all. But the poet shrugs: he was banished to the south and is happy just to be alive. His dream of high office ended long ago, so even a god's blessing is of no use. These lines laugh at himself a little, and also show his stubborn pride and hurt. At the end he spends the night at the monastery under hazy stars and moon. He sleeps until the sun is up, and his mood turns calm and open.
